newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurer PZU sale seen postponed until July.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurer PZU sale seen postponed until July.

text.p: The sale of Poland's largest insurer, state-owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen (PZU), is likely to take place in July at the latest rather than in April, as earlier expected, the company's spokesman said on Thursday.

Marek Maszek told Reuters the first phase of the sale, envisaging a private placement of up to 50 percent in the firm, had to be postponed because of delays in choosing a privatisation adviser and preparing the firm's financial assessment.

"We would like to do it (the sale) by the end of July at the latest...it turned out that it was not such an easy job when such a big company is concerned, and now we are holding talks with investors, which will also take some time," he said.

The company plans a new share issue of 250-750 million zlotys for selected institutional investors, domestic and foreign. Under the plan, each of the investors will have no more than 10-15 percent of the shares.
PZU earlier said it was interested in attracting investors such as the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and leading Polish banks..
The next stage of its privatisation envisages the company's listing on the stock exchange in Warsaw and possibly in London and is likely to take place next year.
PZU had a net loss of 92.9 million zlotys on 3.5-billion-zloty gross premiums last year.
